Each two-story building offers 425,000 gross square feet, including 200,000 square feet of data center space. Initial Ready for Service is targeted for Q2 2026. What does it take to build 3.4 million square feet of AI-ready infrastructure? Our specific construction numbers tell the story. By the Numbers: The Scale of Construction The infrastructure going into the ground reveals just how massive this project is. The electrical backbone: 19,008 power whips requiring over a million feet of Sealtite conduit (198 miles, enough to stretch from Austin to Dallas). The copper wire inside those whips totals 990 miles (enough to stretch from New York City to Jacksonville, Florida). The fiber optic network: 1,760,000 feet of 864-count fiber optic cable (333 miles of high-density fiber). If you connected each individual strand end-to-end, the result would wrap around the Earth 11.5 times. sourceEvidence.excerpt: About | Overview | Freeport LNG Freeport LNG: Clean Energy. Sustainable Solutions. About Freeport LNG Freeport LNG: Taking U.S. Natural Gas Global The shale gas revolution in the late 2000s marked a turning point in the U.S. oil and gas industry. For Freeport LNG, it meant taking our business in a new direction: transforming an import terminal into a natural gas liquefaction and liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility. We are now one of the largest exporters of LNG in the U.S. and the world. What Makes Freeport LNG Successful? A Bright Future. Freeport LNG's three train, 17 MTPA liquefaction facility is the largest all-electric drive motor plant of its kind in the world, making it the most environmentally sustainable site of its kind. The facility’s electric drive motors reduce carbon emissions by over 90% relative to gas turbine-driven liquefaction facilities. Freeport plans to expand by adding a fourth liquefaction train, which has received all regulatory approvals for construction. Freeport was formed in 2002 to develop, own and operate an LNG terminal on Quintana Island, near Freeport, Texas. The terminal started LNG import operations in June 2008 and began LNG export operations in 2019. An additional LNG train (Train 4) is under development. Good Business Inside and Out. Sweetwater 1 (1,400MW) and Sweetwater 2 (600MW) form part of IREN’s announced >5GW global data center development portfolio. judgements.rationale: 2026-08-27 MISO ERAS 원장의 정확한 신청 E0006는 GIA Status=Executed/Filed다. 따라서 계약 체결 단계 50점 추정을 적용한다. Request Status=Active는 연구 절차 상태이며 Done을 발전소 상업운전으로 바꾸지 않는다. Post GIA Status=Not started는 전체 접속절차 미진행을 뜻하지 않는다. Minnesota PUC는 Sandhill과 Crane을 독립 사업으로 구분하며 2026-04 최종 허가를 게재했다. ERAS E0006의 Sandhill/Olmsted/200MW 요약으로 동일성을 대조했다. 인접 Crane의 용량이나 진척을 합치지 않는다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
계약 체결 원장에 철회가 없고 후속 공사/서비스 제공이 예정된 이 신규 접속·증설 요청을 활성으로 해석한다. 기존 모시설이 운영 중이어도 추가 요청을 동일시하지 않는다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
Executed/Filed는 공식 결합 상태로서 접속계약 체결/제출을 확인하지만 FERC 최종 수리 여부는 별도로 단정하지 않는다.
ERAS Max Summer/Winter MW와 Requested ERIS/NRIS MW는 서로 다른 수치다. 기존 용량을 이 평가 작업에서 임의로 변경하지 않는다.
공식 허가 페이지의 두 인접 사업 중 Sandhill만 연결한다. 같은 사건에 포함된 Crane 전체 진척을 E0006에 대신 적용하지 않는다.
judgements.identityRationale: 기존 원장 sourceRecordId=MISO::E0006의 MISO 신청번호를 신규 공식 원문 동일 Project Number/Application ID에 정확 연결했다. 회사명 또는 용량 유사성으로 연결하지 않았다.

sourceEvidence.name: MISO ERAS Informational Guide
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The first quarterly study will kick off on September 2, 2025. There are four ERAS study periods in each year: March-May, June-August, September-November, December-February. To be considered a valid ERAS request and accepted into a cycle, an IR must meet all ERAS requirements prior to the cycle kickoff date. Requirements include 100% generator and ICIF site control, RERRA verification, off-take agreement, application fee and NRIS. ERAS acceptance is not proof that all permits or construction are complete.

sourceEvidence.name: Minnesota PUC: Crane and Sandhill Battery Energy Storage Projects
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Sandhill: independent 200 MW/800 MWh BESS on about 42.7 acres in Olmsted County. Status active. Final Order and Permit 04/22/2026. Sandhill construction anticipated third quarter 2027. The Crane project and Sandhill project are marketed separately.

sourceEvidence.name: MISO ERAS Informational Guide
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The first quarterly study will kick off on September 2, 2025. There are four ERAS study periods in each year: March-May, June-August, September-November, December-February. To be considered a valid ERAS request and accepted into a cycle, an IR must meet all ERAS requirements prior to the cycle kickoff date. Requirements include 100% generator and ICIF site control, RERRA verification, off-take agreement, application fee and NRIS. ERAS acceptance is not proof that all permits or construction are complete.

judgements.rationale: 2026-08-27 MISO ERAS 원장의 정확한 신청 E0012는 GIA Status=Executed/Filed다. 따라서 계약 체결 단계 50점 추정을 적용한다. Request Status=Done는 연구 절차 상태이며 Done을 발전소 상업운전으로 바꾸지 않는다. Post GIA Status=미기재는 전체 접속절차 미진행을 뜻하지 않는다. PSC 9837-CE-100과 Somers의 2026-07 청문 공고 및 WPR 보도를 대조했다. 같은 케노샤·Paris·Invenergy 사업이며 인허가 절차가 별도로 남아 있어 계약 체결을 공사 착수로 올리지 않는다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
계약 체결 원장에 철회가 없고 후속 공사/서비스 제공이 예정된 이 신규 접속·증설 요청을 활성으로 해석한다. 기존 모시설이 운영 중이어도 추가 요청을 동일시하지 않는다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
Executed/Filed는 공식 결합 상태로서 접속계약 체결/제출을 확인하지만 FERC 최종 수리 여부는 별도로 단정하지 않는다.
ERAS Max Summer/Winter MW와 Requested ERIS/NRIS MW는 서로 다른 수치다. 기존 용량을 이 평가 작업에서 임의로 변경하지 않는다.

sourceEvidence.name: InkFreeNews: NIPSCO gas plant filing at Schahfer
sourceEvidence.excerpt: NIPSCO filed plans with IDEM September 22 to construct a 2,300 MW facility at the R.M. Schahfer Generating Station in Wheatfield. Proposal calls for combined-cycle combustion turbines and heat recovery steam units. This expands on a separate announced natural gas peaker.

judgements.rationale: 2026-08-27 MISO ERAS 원장의 정확한 신청 E0043는 GIA Status=Executed/Filed다. 따라서 계약 체결 단계 50점 추정을 적용한다. Request Status=Active는 연구 절차 상태이며 Done을 발전소 상업운전으로 바꾸지 않는다. Post GIA Status=Not started는 전체 접속절차 미진행을 뜻하지 않는다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
계약 체결 원장에 철회가 없고 후속 공사/서비스 제공이 예정된 이 신규 접속·증설 요청을 활성으로 해석한다. 기존 모시설이 운영 중이어도 추가 요청을 동일시하지 않는다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
Executed/Filed는 공식 결합 상태로서 접속계약 체결/제출을 확인하지만 FERC 최종 수리 여부는 별도로 단정하지 않는다.
ERAS Max Summer/Winter MW와 Requested ERIS/NRIS MW는 서로 다른 수치다. 기존 용량을 이 평가 작업에서 임의로 변경하지 않는다.

sourceEvidence.name: MISO ERAS Informational Guide
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The first quarterly study will kick off on September 2, 2025. There are four ERAS study periods in each year: March-May, June-August, September-November, December-February. To be considered a valid ERAS request and accepted into a cycle, an IR must meet all ERAS requirements prior to the cycle kickoff date. Requirements include 100% generator and ICIF site control, RERRA verification, off-take agreement, application fee and NRIS. ERAS acceptance is not proof that all permits or construction are complete.

judgements.rationale: MISO의 E0044가 Active이고 배정 주기는 ERAS Study Cycle 4다. 첫 ERAS 주기는 2025-09 시작, 이후 분기별이라는 공식 안내에 따라 2026-08-27 원장 시점에서 2026-06~08 연구 주기 참여로 판단해 80점을 추정한다. GIA 체결은 미공개이므로 가정하지 않는다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
개별 연구 산출물 대신 공식 주기 배정과 Active 상태를 종합해 주기상 연구/대기 위치를 추정한다. 실제 기술 공정률을 계측한 값은 아니다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
원장 기준일 후 예정된 분기 시작일이 지났다는 이유만으로 현재 단계가 진척됐다고 자동 갱신하지 않는다.
ERAS Max Summer/Winter MW와 Requested ERIS/NRIS MW는 서로 다른 수치다. 기존 용량을 이 평가 작업에서 임의로 변경하지 않는다.

sourceEvidence.name: MISO ERAS Informational Guide
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The first quarterly study will kick off on September 2, 2025. There are four ERAS study periods in each year: March-May, June-August, September-November, December-February. To be considered a valid ERAS request and accepted into a cycle, an IR must meet all ERAS requirements prior to the cycle kickoff date. Requirements include 100% generator and ICIF site control, RERRA verification, off-take agreement, application fee and NRIS. ERAS acceptance is not proof that all permits or construction are complete.

judgements.bottleneck: 수정 계통영향 연구 및 접속설비 시설연구(FS)
judgements.rationale: 공식 API에서 동일 신청 J3485의 DPP-2023 / East (ITC) / Phase 2가 확인된다. MISO 절차 정의상 수정 계통영향 연구 및 접속설비 시설연구(FS) 단계이므로 70점 모형을 적용한다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
API에 별도 문서 기준일이 없으므로 asOf는 현재 상태를 실제 조회한 날짜다. 과거 그 날짜에 단계가 전환됐다는 뜻이 아니다.
judgements.identityRationale: 기존 원장 sourceRecordId=MISO::J3485의 MISO 신청번호를 신규 공식 원문 동일 Project Number/Application ID에 정확 연결했다. 회사명 또는 용량 유사성으로 연결하지 않았다.

judgements.bottleneck: 수정 계통영향 연구 및 접속설비 시설연구(FS)
judgements.rationale: 공식 API에서 동일 신청 J3602의 DPP-2023 / Central / Phase 2가 확인된다. MISO 절차 정의상 수정 계통영향 연구 및 접속설비 시설연구(FS) 단계이므로 70점 모형을 적용한다. 신청 상태는 Pending Transfer로, 철회가 아닌 변경 승인/명의 이전 대기 중 활성 신청이라는 해석을 추가한다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
Pending Revision Approval 또는 Pending Transfer는 철회하지 않은 진행 신청으로 해석한다. 변경 승인 여부 자체가 기술 연구 완료를 뜻하지 않는다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
API에 별도 문서 기준일이 없으므로 asOf는 현재 상태를 실제 조회한 날짜다. 과거 그 날짜에 단계가 전환됐다는 뜻이 아니다.
judgements.identityRationale: 기존 원장 sourceRecordId=MISO::J3602의 MISO 신청번호를 신규 공식 원문 동일 Project Number/Application ID에 정확 연결했다. 회사명 또는 용량 유사성으로 연결하지 않았다.

projectSnapshot.name: Replacing 864 MW of coal with Natural Gas Generators; Castle Bluff

judgements.rationale: MISO R1047의 Castle Bluff/Meramec 접속점은 연구 Done이지만, Ameren의 2026-02 건설 착수 보도와 2026-05 첫 터빈 현장 반입이 실제 후속 공사를 확인한다. 기존 Meramec 부지를 활용하는 새 Castle Bluff 발전소 공사로 25점 추정을 부여한다. 2027 운영 목표는 현재 운영 승인으로 해석하지 않는다.
assumptions: 배점은 공개 절차를 공통 단계 모형으로 해석한 추정이며 다섯 독립 요건의 실제 공정률이 아니다.
확인된 공사 착수·터빈 반입과 현재 사업자 페이지의 후속 일정을 근거로 계속 진행 중이라고 해석한다. 이후 전면 운영·철회 사실은 확보되지 않았다.
limitations: 기존 LBNL 용량과 원문 상태는 수정하지 않는다. 신규 원문 용량·요청 서비스 MW의 차이는 별도 용량 재검토 대상이다.
발표된 운전 목표일을 실제 통전·상업운전일로 바꾸지 않는다.
judgements.identityRationale: MISO R1047의 기존 명칭 Castle Bluff, Missouri/St. Louis County, Meramec 138kV 접속점과 Ameren 공식 신규 Castle Bluff 부지/발전방식이 일치한다. 기존 Meramec 석탄 발전소 또는 별도 Castle Bluff BESS가 아니다.

The Kingston Substation is needed to reliably serve the newly approved Cedar Crossing Casino and Entertainment Center.
IPL has notified ITC that they will be constructing a new Kingston Substation which will ultimately replace their existing Harrison substation. sourceEvidence.name: MISO Projects Under Evaluation / MTEP 51145
sourceEvidence.excerpt:
MTEP Project ID: 51145
New Crossroads 345 kV Transmission Station and Load
To connect a new 300 MW load, it is necessary to construct a new transmission station and interconnect the described transmission lines.
Construct a new 345 kV breaker and a half station and interconnect a new 300 MW (98.61 MVAR) load approximately 3 miles northwest of Carlisle, Indiana.

The new station will bring the existing Gibson – Merom 345 kV, Merom – Worthington 345 kV, and Petersburg – Sullivan 345 kV lines into a new BAAH station. Extending the Merom – Worthington 345 kV line through the site requires the construction of approximately 10 new miles of 345 kV line.

These lines are currently being modified in the existing MTEP 51093 project where they are being brought into the new Gill 345 kV station. This will result in a final topology for these branches being as follows:
1.	Gibson – Crossroads – J1786 – Gill – Merom
2.	Petersburg – Crossroads – Gill – Sullivan
3.	Worthington – Crossroads – Gill - Merom
Planning Status: M2 - Appendix A Approved
Expected ISD: 2027-10-01 00:00:00

New Gill 345 kV Station and 345 kV Lines
To serve expanding data center load.

Construct a second 345 kV line from Merom Station to Gill Station. 

Remove the following 345 kV line terminations from Merom station and terminate them at Gill station instead:

•	345kV Line from Duke Gibson

Modify existing LRTP project to bring the IPL Sullivan-Petersburg 345kV line into Gill station instead of Merom station.  

As part of this EPR, the following additional data center loads are being added at the Gill bus:
•	960 MW by 1/1/2028. This is in addition to the loads already modeled at this bus in MTEP25 models.

Expected ISD: 2028-01-01 00:00:00

MTEP Project ID: 51307
New Hackman Phase 1 Load addition
To connect a new 300 MW load, it is necessary to construct a new transmission station and interconnect the described transmission lines.
Construct a new 345 kV breaker-and-a-half transmission station on the 345 kV line between Prescott and Gwynneville east of Shelbyville to serve a new large load. The initial load is planned to grow to 300 MW (98.6 MVAR).
Planning Status: M1 - Proposed
Expected ISD: 2028-06-01 00:00:00
[…]
MTEP Project ID: 51308
New Hackman Phase 2 Load addition
To connect a new 600 MW load, it is necessary to construct a new transmission station and interconnect the described transmission lines.
Expand Hoosier Energy's Milroy 69 kV station with a new 345 kV breaker and a half station called Rush County that interconnects with the 345 kV line between Hanna and Tanners Creek (between Gwynneville and Batesville after LRTP Tranche 2.1). Construct a new 14 mile 345 kV double circuit from Rush County to the Hackman station east of Shelbyville. Construct a new 69 kV line from the expanded Milroy station to Hoosier Pioneer 69 kV substation. Interconnect additional 600 MW (197.2 MVAR) at Hackman 345 kV station.
Planning Status: M1 - Proposed
Expected ISD: 2030-06-01 00:00:00

sourceEvidence.name: Lilly Medicine Foundry official groundbreaking account
sourceEvidence.excerpt: That’s where the Lilly Medicine Foundry comes in. We recently broke ground on the facility, a state-of-the-art location combining research, process development, manufacturing, and the latest technology at a single site. Located in Lebanon, Indiana, the Foundry will enable us to research new, optimized ways of producing medicines to help scale global access to clinical trials supply, while reducing environmental impact. The flexible design of the Foundry will support various molecular therapies, including small molecules, biologics and next-generation therapeutics like genetic medicines. This will allow us to meet the needs of complex conditions, like Alzheimer’s disease and chronic pain. The Foundry’s strategic location in the LEAP Lebanon Innovation District will offer close collaboration with other Lilly product development teams in Indianapolis and manufacturing sites in Lebanon to drive faster and smarter innovation across our company.

To accommodate the requested load interconnection, 4 new 161 kV bus positions need to be added on the DAEC 161 kV bus to facilitate interconnection of the 4 new CIPCO radial 161 kV lines to the new load.  No other upgrades were identified as being required to support the requested load interconnection.
Central Iowa Power Cooperative (CIPCO) on behalf of its member Linn County Rural Electric Cooperative (Linn County REC) has requested to interconnect a new 620 MW load that will be served from the Duane Arnold Energy Center (DAEC) 161 kV bus via four new radial 161 kV lines that will be owned and operated by CIPCO.  To accommodate the requested load interconnection, ITC Midwest will expand the 161 kV bus at DAEC to provide 4 additional 161 kV bus positions.

Riddle 230 kV Station and Line Upgrade
Entergy received a request from a customer adding new load near St Francisville, LA.  These facilities were identified as needed due to the load growth.

Entergy is proposing to construct a new 230 kV station named Riddle to serve a new customer cut into the existing Fancy Point to Ventress 230 kV line near Saint Francisville, LA.

The Riddle 230 kV station will be a breaker and a half substation. The new station has a target ISD in June 2026.

The need to reconductor the Fancy Point to Riddle 230 kV line was also identified to serve this load.

Expected ISD: 2026-05-18 00:00:00

Currently, there are an estimated 8,500 workers on the site, daily. Construction using 28,000 tons of domestically sourced steel , along with other U.S.-made materials. Each of the seven data center buildings will begin operations with an amount of cooling water equivalent to an Olympic-sized swimming pool. They will employ a closed-loop cooling system, so ongoing water consumption will be minimal. Since breaking ground last May, more than 8.5 million work hours have been expended. Construction is expected to be completed within 16 months. Facts provided by QTS.

projectSnapshot.name: AVAIO Project Leo
projectSnapshot.rawStatus: Type Turnkey or Powered Shell Location 145th Street, Little Rock, Pulaski County, AR Latitude & Longitude 34.623375 -92.246825 Acreage 296 acres 1,070 MW Total Baseload Power 570 MW Total Grid Power 500 MW Total Baseload BTM "AVAIO's campus is a generational investment in the power and digital infrastructure Arkansas needs to compete globally. Pulaski County Judge, Barry Hyde "AVAIO Digital's $6 billion data center hub represents the largest economic investment in Arkansas' history and sets the Natural State up to become a technology powerhouse that can compete with any state in the nation.” Governor, Sarah Huckabee Sanders AVAIO has broken ground on Project Leo, a 296-acre project with an initial fully contracted capacity online by 2027. The site, less than ten miles from downtown Little Rock, has a fully approved Site Plan with substantial existing on-site water and sewer infrastructure: ‍ Executed ESA with Entergy Arkansas for an initial grid capacity energized in Q4 2027, priced competitively with the lowest-cost power markets in the US ‍ Existing fiber networks along the adjacent rights-of-way can be accessed by four non-single-point-of-failure campus fiber entry points. Pre-existing water and sewer connections provide significant water and wastewater capacity availability with no required upgrades, and the State of Arkansas offers substantial Sales and Use Tax incentives for data center tenants, reducing total cost of ownership on qualifying capital expenditures. Turnkey, build-to-suit, and powered shell options are available.

projectSnapshot.name: Google West Memphis data center
projectSnapshot.rawStatus:
Google is good for Arkansas
  and great for Entergy customers
  Google is investing $4 billion on cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure in
  Arkansas, including the development of a new data center in West Memphis
  – the company’s first facility in the state – powered by Entergy.
  Their historic investment in our state is bringing unparalleled benefits that will
  improve the lives of Arkansans for generations to come.


How will it benefit you?
           High tech partner = Lower cost power
           Google will cover the full energy costs associated with powering the facility, which will produce more
           than $1 billion in net customer savings over the life of the contract. In addition, as a new large industrial
           customer on our grid, Google will pick up more of the grid maintenance improvement costs that existing
           customers would otherwise have to bear alone and at a larger share than residential and small
           business customers.
           Adding any power-intensive facility to our grid can raise questions about its impact on service reliability
           for other customers, but we’ve ensured that our power service agreement with Google not only protects
           reliability for all customers, it improves it through measures such as:
           • Adding a new solar generation and battery storage facility in Jefferson County financially supported
             by Google.
           • Electrical infrastructure additions and improvements that will enhance reliability of the entire grid and
             lower costs for all customers.
           • A program to reduce data center power use during peak hours to support grid stability for all customers.

sourceEvidence.name: Axios New Orleans: River Bend on-site construction visit, October 5
sourceEvidence.excerpt: As Hut 8 site manager Brennan Church sat at the front of the bus, he quipped that this project was "the first time I've had to deal with alligators on a construction site." He pointed out the infrastructure his team carved out of forested hunting land off a dead-end road near St. Francisville. There's the substation and a switchyard to manage the Entergy Louisiana power as it comes on site, and the equipment it takes to safely isolate the data center from the larger regional grid. There's the trestle bridge system crossing a field of rolling hills dotted with rebar and cranes to connect all that power, using 762,000 linear feet of cable, directly to the enormous data center itself. It'll take 1.5 million gallons of propylene glycol to keep it cool on a closed-loop system, Hut 8's Collier Pruner says, without having to draw on local water. In all, it's taking about 1,200 construction crew members working 24/7 to bring Hut 8's data center online by the first quarter of 2027, with full completion expected throughout next year.

sourceEvidence.name: Wisconsin PSC: Ozaukee distribution interconnection application
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Application Summary Overview American Transmission Company (ATC or applicant) is seeking approval to construct new 345 kV and 138 kV transmission lines and 4 to 5 substations in the counties of Calumet, Fond du Lac, Ozaukee, Manitowoc, Sheboygan and Washington. The project is divided into two geographic parts: the north scope and south scope. In the north scope, both the North West and North East routes include one new 345kV transmission line that originates at the Forest Junction substation in Calumet County and travels south to the proposed Sheboygan River Substation in Fond du Lac County. In the south scope, the South East and South West Route would include a 345kV transmission line that would connect the proposed Mullet River Junction Substation, run south connecting to several intermediary substations, before terminating at the proposed Cedar Creek Junction in the Town of Jackson. Both routes would include a Common Route, consisting of two new 345kV transmission lines running parallel east to west to connect to the proposed intermediary Decker Substation in Port Washington. The proposed Decker Substation would also include the installation and connection of an Enhanced STATCOM (Static Synchronous Compensator) adjacent to it. The South East Route also would include building two new 138kV transmission circuits to connect to the proposed intermediary Adell Substation in Sherman Center and the existing Holland Substation.​

projectSnapshot.name: TeraWulf Justified Data Campus
projectSnapshot.rawStatus:
TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF) (“TeraWulf” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated owner, developer and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure, today announced that the Kentucky Public Service Commission (“PSC”) has approved the Retail Electric Service Agreement (“RESA”) supporting up to 482 megawatts (“MW”) of electric service for TeraWulf’s Justified Data Campus in Hancock County, Kentucky. The approval represents an important milestone for Justified and, in TeraWulf’s view, validates a strong model for responsible large-scale data center development: securing substantial power capacity while ensuring that project-specific costs and risks are borne by the large-load customer, protecting existing ratepayers and creating incremental value for utilities and local communities. In its August 21, 2026 order, the Commission concluded: “After consideration of the entire record, the Commission finds that the proposed RESA contains adequate protections for existing customers, appropriately allocates financial and operational risks, establishes rates that are fair, just and reasonable, and provides for adequate and reliable service.” Under the approved structure, TeraWulf is responsible for the market, transmission, delivery and other costs attributable to serving its load, together with customer-specific infrastructure costs and substantial credit-support obligations.
[…]
The agreement also includes negotiated demand adders and customer charges that provide incremental contributions to Big Rivers Electric Corporation (“Big Rivers”) and Kenergy Corp.
[…]
The Justified Data Campus is being developed at the former Century Aluminum Hawesville facility, where approximately 482 MW of existing transmission capability remains available following the closure of the aluminum smelter.

judgements.rationale: TeraWulf가 2026-08-21 Kentucky PSC의 단일 Justified RESA 승인을 명시하고 최대 482 MW를 확보했습니다. 옛 제련소 송전 용량 재사용은 새 데이터센터 운영을 입증하지 않으므로 계약 체결 단계로 판단합니다.
assumptions: 모든 요건별 진행률과 점수는 공통 정성 모형의 가정이며 직접 확인한 공정률이 아닙니다.

Oracle and BorderPlex Digital Assets today announced Project Jupiter will utilize Bloom Energy fuel cells to fully power the AI data center campus in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. As part of Oracle and Bloom’s previously announced expanded partnership, the data center will be supported by up to 2.45 GW of installed Bloom fuel cell capacity. This updated power design will replace Project Jupiter’s previously planned gas turbines and diesel generators and consolidate the facility into one single microgrid campus. Fuel cells generate electricity without combustion, meaning the Bloom microgrid is highly efficient with low emissions and water use. projectSnapshot.rawStatus: ESA negotiated and executed; Commission approval application under Modified Procedure, public comments due December 17, 2026

judgements.bottleneck: 공급계약 서명 후 규제 승인 대기
judgements.rationale: Idaho PUC IPC-E-26-19는 Chobani 증설을 위한 ESA가 협상·서명됐고 고객이 접속 시설 선투자 비용을 부담한다고 명시합니다. 2026-09-08 명령은 최종 승인 대신 Modified Procedure로 진행하므로 계약 미완료/규제 승인 대기로 판단합니다.
assumptions: 서명된 공급 약정과 접속 비용 부담 의무는 단순 신청 이후의 상업적 진척으로 평가합니다.
계약 서명을 다섯 요건 전체의 완료나 최종 통전 승인으로 취급하지 않습니다.
limitations: 기존 공장 운영분과 새 증설 부하를 구분합니다. 기존 공장이 가동 중이라는 이유로 증설 접속을 0점 처리하지 않습니다.
최종 승인·증설 설비의 전력공사·통전은 확인하지 못했습니다.
judgements.identityRationale: 공개 원장의 동일 서비스/신청 번호를 기존 원문 ID와 정확히 연결했습니다. 회사명이나 용량 유사성만으로 합치지 않았습니다.

judgements.bottleneck: 비용배분 거절 후 다음 시설검토 대기
judgements.rationale: NYISO 1315는 이미 비용배분 결정을 받을 정도로 검토를 진행했고 이를 거절해 다음 FS를 기다리는 상태입니다. 초기 미진행으로 되돌려 100점을 주지 않고 시설검토 대기 모형 75점으로 해석합니다.
assumptions: FS는 NYISO 단계 범례의 Facilities Study이며 이전 검토 실적과 재검토 대기가 공존하는 상태로 해석합니다.
거절된 비용배분을 수용한 것으로 처리하지 않아 계약 체결 단계 점수는 주지 않습니다.

sourceEvidence.name: SPP 상세 연구 Sofidel — Rocky Point
sourceEvidence.excerpt:
This report outlines the results of an evaluation of regional transmission impacts from delivery point request DPA-2026-May-2350. The requesting entity plans to add new load (Sofidel) to the existing delivery point called Rocky Point with an in-service date of 6/1/2028. The Rocky Point delivery point is in the American Electric Power (AEP) Transmission System. The load flow models used for the evaluation were 2026 Integrated Transmission Planning (ITP) base reliability models. Southwest Power Pool (SPP) performed an Alternating Current (AC) contingency analysis on these models using PSS®E. DPA-2026-May-2350 Publication August 10, 2026/Version 1 1 SECTION 2: STUDY METHODOLOGY OBJECTIVE The purpose of this study was to determine the regional Transmission System impacts within the SPP footprint due to the new load served by AEP. SPP performed a Delivery Point Network Study (DPNS) with the configurations shown in Table 2-1 below. STUDY PROCESS • Model Assumptions o 2026 ITP Base Reliability Model Series ▪ Model years 2028, 2030, and 2035 ▪ Summer Peak (2028S, 2030S, and 2035S), Winter Peak (2028W, 2030W, and 2035W), Summer Shoulder (203
Section 4 Conclusion: The AC analysis revealed potential thermal and voltage violations associated with the Sofidel load addition. The study shows that the following upgrades are required to reliably serve the load addition: Rebuild Locust Grove to Moonlight 115 kV circuit 1; Alto 138 kV 1 MVAR capacitor bank.

The purpose of this study was to determine the regional transmission system impacts within the SPP footprint associated with the addition of a new, 816 MW data center load in the Clarksville area served by Clarksville Connected Utilities (CCU). The study modeled an initial 18 MW load and an expanded load of 798 MW (total 816 MW) in the 2029 and 2034 model years. The load was interconnected at the existing 69 kV CLRKSVL2 station (Bus 505511) and the proposed 161 kV Substation Alpha - Clarksville Bravo station (Bus 505996). The new delivery point and associated facilities are intended to support a phased data center development near Clarksville, Arkansas. In the 2029 Light Load model, the modeled expanded load was reduced to 667 MW instead of 798 MW to reflect the expected loading conditions for that seasonal scenario. To accommodate the proposed Clarksville load addition, additional generation resources were added in the surrounding area to support system p

After additional DNH study by PJM, a generation deliverability overload was found at Gosney Hill 138kV station on the Gosney Hill- Nauvoo Ridge 138 kV line for loss of the Kammer-Panhandle 500 kV line and the Kammer 765/500 kV transformer ('AEP_P1- 3_#8975_05KAMMER 765_200‘, 'AEP_P1-2_500-1‘). Estimated Cost: $4.8 M Rebuild the Kammer-Natrium 138kV double-circuit line (9.3 miles). The circuit’s limiting ratings are currently set by the T-Line conductor (556 ACSR). sourceEvidence.name: PJM M-3 AEP-2021-OH049 row 495
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 495; Need Number AEP-2021-OH049; Need Meeting Date 2023-02-17 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2023-12-05 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3441; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: Jerome Delivery Point (UREC) 138 kV: • Buckeye Power Inc., on behalf of Union Rural Electric Cooperative Inc., has requested new transmission service in Plain City, Ohio. • The delivery point will be used to serve a customer with high potential for rapid load growth. The initial load will be 62.5 106 MW with a potential future peak load demand of 244 MW. • Service is requested by January 2025 June 2024. • The customer recently communicated a much more aggressive load ramp/build out schedule that would put their peak load at approximately 160 MW by early 2025 at the site. This Need was originally presented as a Buckeye Power request; The customer has since requested service from AEP Ohio at the site. As part of this request, the customer has indicated the need for additional feeds at the delivery which will bring the load amount up to 203 MW.; Solution Description: The following scope of work is all direct connect facilities to physically connect demand to the grid. • Jerome 138 kV: Construct a greenfield Jerome station with (11) 138kV 63kA 4000A circuit breakers in breaker and half bus configuration. Construct ~ 2.5 miles of double circuit 138kV transmission line extending from Celtic & Kileville stations utilizing 2-bundled ACSS Cardinal 954 (45/7) conductor, SE rating 1061 MVA. Construct ~1.6 miles of double circuit 138kV transmission line extending from Jerome to cut-in back to Hyatt – Amlin line utilizing 2-bundled ACSS Cardinal 954 (45/7) conductor, SE rating 1061 MVA. Construct (4) 138 kV tie lines to the customers dead end structures ~0.05 miles utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor SE 284 MVA. Customers will be directly connected at this station. Cost: $30 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Beatty – Wilson 138 kV line Sag Re-rate: Due to new customer interconnections in the area the Beatty – Wilson, Beatty – Bolton, Bolton – Hall and Hall - Wilson 138 kV circuits will overload for certain N-1-1 scenarios. Structures will be replaced on the line to address distribution clearance issue in order to allow the lines to operate to their conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.5 M • Dublin Reactor 138 kV: Install a 4% series reactor towards Sawmill at Dublin station to address a N-1-1 scenario as a result of the new load interconnections in the area. Cost: $3.0 M

sourceEvidence.name: PJM M-3 AEP-2021-OH061 row 502
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 502; Need Number AEP-2021-OH061; Need Meeting Date 2021-11-19 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2022-01-21 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date 2022-04-25 00:00:00; Local Plan Year 2022; PJM Upgrade ID s2688; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: Customer Service: AEP Ohio has requested a new load delivery point due to capacity loading limits at the Barnesville 69/12kV substation. The station is limited by its power transformer and secondary cables. The transformer was manufactured in 1968, has poor oil quality, and has bushing issues reported. Operational Flexibility and Efficiency: The station is served radially via a 0.4-mile 69kV tap. This T-line tap dates back to 1942, with original #1 copper conductor, and currently has 2 open conditions. Other projects in the area have proposed to rebuild the remainder of the 69 kV line in the area. Barnesville has an obsolete MOAB/ground-switch for the transformer protection system. This requires remote-end breaker clearing many miles away, and drops another tapped AEP Ohio distribution station in the process (Batesville).; Solution Description: Install a new distribution station (“Pumpkin”) adjacent to the 69kV transmission through-path south of Barnesville. Retire Barnesville station. Estimated Cost $0.83 Million (does not include Distribution costs for the station) Retire the 0.4-mile 69kV transmission line tap into Barnesville station. Estimated Cost: $0.46 Million Loop the Speidel-Summerfield 69kV transmission line into Pumpkin station. Estimated Cost: $1.38 Million

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 576; Need Number AEP-2022-OH023; Need Meeting Date 2022-01-21 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2023-12-05 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3442; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: Customer Service: • A customer has requested transmission service at a site North of AEP’s existing Jugg Street station in Columbus, OH. • The customer has indicated an initial peak demand of 90 125 MW with an ultimate capacity of up to 360 290 MW at the site. • Initial customer requested in-service date of June 1, 2024; Solution Description: Badger 138 kV: Cut into the Green Chapel – Jug 138 kV circuit and extend ~ 0.1 miles of new double circuit line, utilizing 2-bundled ACSR Falcon 1590 (54/19) conductor, SE rating 1118 MVA , to the greenfield Badger station with (10) 80 kA, 4000 A breakers & (1) 69.1 MVAR 138 kV Cap bank, laid out as breaker and a half for future expansion to 6 strings. Construct 4 - 138 kV tie lines to the customers dead end structures ~.05 miles utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor SE 284 MVA. Cost: $18.43 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Corridor – Vassell 345 kV #1 & #2 Circuits Sag Re-rate: Replace two structures to mitigate sag issues on the line in order to allow the line to operate to its conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.88 M • Kiber Station 138 kV: Cut-into Green Chapel – Corridor 138 kV circuit to a new Kiber station with (8 3) 80 kA 138 kV circuit breakers laid out in a breaker and a half arrangement to install a 300 2x150 MVAR STATCOM to support the significant amount of load added to the area. Cost: $35 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering analysis it was determined that in order to be able to physically accommodate the line exits along with two feeds to the STATCOM when taking into account future needs at the station that a total of 8 138 kV breakers would need to be installed initially. • Green Chapel Cap Banks 138 kV: Upgrade proposed cap banks at Green Chapel station from (2) 69.1 MVAR to (2) 115.2 MVAR. Cost: $3.6 M • Corridor 138 kV: Replace (12) 63 kA circuit breakers & cap breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $12.6 M • Babbitt 138 kV: Replace (2) 63 kA bus-tie circuit breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $2.15 M • Jug Street: Replace CB-C which is an existing 40 kA breaker with a 4000A 80kA 138 kV breaker to address interrupting capability concerns related to the introduction of the new 345 kV source at Innovation. Cost: $0.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Anchor Hocking – Lancaster 69 kV line Rebuild: Rebuild ~1.16 miles of 69 kV line utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor, SE 142 MVA. As a result of the new customer interconnections in the area, this line will overload under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Newark Center 138 kV: Install high and low side sectionalizing on the 138/69 kV transformer to address overloading of 69 kV lines in the area related to the new customer interconnections under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Fremont – West Fremont Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit & upgrade 1200 A switches at Fremont to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $2.0 M • Fremont – Fremont Center Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $1.5 M • Dumont 765 kV: Replace 3000 A circuit breaker at Dumont to address a generation deliverability violation on the Dumont – Sorenson 765 kV branch related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $4.0 M The following components are system reinforcements that were initially identified by AEP and later confirmed by PJM through their DNH analysis: • Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Green Chapel stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell – Curleys 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Curleys stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell 765 & 345 kV stations: Add 3-345 kV breakers to connect new lines to Curleys and Green Chapel. Cost: $10 M • Green Chapel 345/138 kV station: Install two 675 MVA, 345/138 kV transformers to connect the new Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line to 138 kV system and to mitigate overloading on the other 345/138 kV transformers in the system. Cost: $39.2 M System Upgrades: $199.2 M

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 587; Need Number AEP-2022-OH034; Need Meeting Date 2022-04-22 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2023-12-05 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3442; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: Customer Service: • A customer has requested transmission service at a site East of AEP’s existing Anguin station in New Albany, OH. • The customer has indicated a peak demand of 144 216 MW at the site. • The customer has requested an ISD of 5/31/2023; Solution Description: The following work is all direct connect substations to physically connect demand to the grid. • QTS North 138 kV: Construct ~0.3 miles of double circuit & a single circuit radial 138 kV tie lines from Anguin station to QTS Customer’s site dead-end structures serving transformers #1, #2 # 3, each utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor SE 284 MVA. Cost: $1.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Corridor – Vassell 345 kV #1 & #2 Circuits Sag Re-rate: Replace two structures to mitigate sag issues on the line in order to allow the line to operate to its conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.88 M • Kiber Station 138 kV: Cut-into Green Chapel – Corridor 138 kV circuit to a new Kiber station with (8 3) 80 kA 138 kV circuit breakers laid out in a breaker and a half arrangement to install a 300 2x150 MVAR STATCOM to support the significant amount of load added to the area. Cost: $35 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering analysis it was determined that in order to be able to physically accommodate the line exits along with two feeds to the STATCOM when taking into account future needs at the station that a total of 8 138 kV breakers would need to be installed initially. • Green Chapel Cap Banks 138 kV: Upgrade proposed cap banks at Green Chapel station from (2) 69.1 MVAR to (2) 115.2 MVAR. Cost: $3.6 M • Corridor 138 kV: Replace (12) 63 kA circuit breakers & cap breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $12.6 M • Babbitt 138 kV: Replace (2) 63 kA bus-tie circuit breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $2.15 M • Jug Street: Replace CB-C which is an existing 40 kA breaker with a 4000A 80kA 138 kV breaker to address interrupting capability concerns related to the introduction of the new 345 kV source at Innovation. Cost: $0.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Anchor Hocking – Lancaster 69 kV line Rebuild: Rebuild ~1.16 miles of 69 kV line utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor, SE 142 MVA. As a result of the new customer interconnections in the area, this line will overload under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Newark Center 138 kV: Install high and low side sectionalizing on the 138/69 kV transformer to address overloading of 69 kV lines in the area related to the new customer interconnections under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Fremont – West Fremont Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit & upgrade 1200 A switches at Fremont to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $2.0 M • Fremont – Fremont Center Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $1.5 M • Dumont 765 kV: Replace 3000 A circuit breaker at Dumont to address a generation deliverability violation on the Dumont – Sorenson 765 kV branch related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $4.0 M The following components are system reinforcements that were initially identified by AEP and later confirmed by PJM through their DNH analysis: • Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Green Chapel stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell – Curleys 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Curleys stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell 765 & 345 kV stations: Add 3-345 kV breakers to connect new lines to Curleys and Green Chapel. Cost: $10 M • Green Chapel 345/138 kV station: Install two 675 MVA, 345/138 kV transformers to connect the new Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line to 138 kV system and to mitigate overloading on the other 345/138 kV transformers in the system. Cost: $39.2 M System Upgrades: $199.2 M

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 589; Need Number AEP-2022-OH036; Need Meeting Date 2022-04-22 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2023-12-05 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3442; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: Customer Service: • The customer served out of Innovation station (S2578) has requested additional transmission service at their existing site just south of the existing Conesville – Corridor 345 kV circuit in New Albany, OH. • The customer has indicated a peak demand of 286.5 247 MW at the site. • The customer has requested an ISD of 4/1/2024; Solution Description: The following work is all direct connect substations to physically connect demand to the grid. • Innovation 345/138 kV: Cut into the Corridor - Conesville 345 kV circuit and construct ~0.1 miles of double circuit line, utilizing 2-bundled ACSR Bittern 1272 conductor, SE rating 2278 MVA, to a new 345 kV ring bus at Innovation station (s2578) with (4) 5000 A, 63kA circuit breakers, (2) 345/138/34.5 kV, 675 MVA transformers, (15) 4000 A, 80, kA, 138 kV circuit breakers, (2) 69.1 MVAR, 138 kV Cap banks. Upgrade the line protection relays at Conesville & Corridor 345 kV. Construct (2) 138 kV tie lines to the customers dead end structures ~0.04 miles utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor SE 284 MVA. Cost: $53.7 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Corridor – Vassell 345 kV #1 & #2 Circuits Sag Re-rate: Replace two structures to mitigate sag issues on the line in order to allow the line to operate to its conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.88 M • Kiber Station 138 kV: Cut-into Green Chapel – Corridor 138 kV circuit to a new Kiber station with (8 3) 80 kA 138 kV circuit breakers laid out in a breaker and a half arrangement to install a 300 2x150 MVAR STATCOM to support the significant amount of load added to the area. Cost: $35 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering analysis it was determined that in order to be able to physically accommodate the line exits along with two feeds to the STATCOM when taking into account future needs at the station that a total of 8 138 kV breakers would need to be installed initially. • Green Chapel Cap Banks 138 kV: Upgrade proposed cap banks at Green Chapel station from (2) 69.1 MVAR to (2) 115.2 MVAR. Cost: $3.6 M • Corridor 138 kV: Replace (12) 63 kA circuit breakers & cap breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $12.6 M • Babbitt 138 kV: Replace (2) 63 kA bus-tie circuit breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $2.15 M • Jug Street: Replace CB-C which is an existing 40 kA breaker with a 4000A 80kA 138 kV breaker to address interrupting capability concerns related to the introduction of the new 345 kV source at Innovation. Cost: $0.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Anchor Hocking – Lancaster 69 kV line Rebuild: Rebuild ~1.16 miles of 69 kV line utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor, SE 142 MVA. As a result of the new customer interconnections in the area, this line will overload under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Newark Center 138 kV: Install high and low side sectionalizing on the 138/69 kV transformer to address overloading of 69 kV lines in the area related to the new customer interconnections under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Fremont – West Fremont Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit & upgrade 1200 A switches at Fremont to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $2.0 M • Fremont – Fremont Center Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $1.5 M • Dumont 765 kV: Replace 3000 A circuit breaker at Dumont to address a generation deliverability violation on the Dumont – Sorenson 765 kV branch related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $4.0 M The following components are system reinforcements that were initially identified by AEP and later confirmed by PJM through their DNH analysis: • Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Green Chapel stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell – Curleys 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Curleys stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell 765 & 345 kV stations: Add 3-345 kV breakers to connect new lines to Curleys and Green Chapel. Cost: $10 M • Green Chapel 345/138 kV station: Install two 675 MVA, 345/138 kV transformers to connect the new Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line to 138 kV system and to mitigate overloading on the other 345/138 kV transformers in the system. Cost: $39.2 M System Upgrades: $199.2 M

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 612; Need Number AEP-2022-OH071; Need Meeting Date 2022-10-14 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 12/5/2023, 2/13/2026; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3440; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes Scope change 2/13/2026; Problem Statement: • A customer has requested additional 138 kV deliveries to their site in Columbus, Ohio near AEP’s proposed Cyprus station (s2526). • The initial peak demand at these new delivery points will be approximately 200 MW and the ultimate capacity of the customer will be up to 675 MW at the site.; Solution Description: The following work is all direct connect facilities to physically connect demand to the grid. • Cyprus 345/138 kV: Cyprus is the station that was originally developed (s2526) to serve 675 MW of demand with room for 345 kV expansion based on LOA with the customer. Cut into the Beatty – Bixby 345 kV circuit and construct ~1.6 miles of double circuit line, utilizing 2-bundled ACSR Bittern 1272 conductor, SE rating 2278 MVA, to a new 345 kV ring bus at Cyprus station with (4) 5000 A, 63kA circuit breakers, (2) 345/138/34.5 kV, 675 MVA transformers, (12) 4000 A, 63kA, 138 kV circuit breakers, (1) 69.1 MVAR 138 kV Cap bank. Construct (2) 138 kV single circuit, ~0.4 miles, & (2) double circuit, ~0.9 miles, tie lines to the customers dead end structures utilizing ACSR Drake 795 (26/7) conductor SE 360 MVA. Modify the existing Cyprus 138kV Extension & Parsons 138kV circuits #1 & 2 structures to accommodate a fence relocation. Remote end relay upgrades are required at Beatty & Bixby 345 kV stations. Cost: $46.9 M • Parsons 138 kV: Install (1) 69.1 MVAR cap bank to resolve N-1-1 voltage issues. Cost: $2.0 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Beatty – Canal 138 kV line Sag Re-rate: The Beatty – Canal 138 kV line flagged as overloading under N-1-1 scenarios after the addition of the new load at Cyprus. The line will be flown to address sag issues that are limiting its current rating. It is anticipated that several structures will need to be replaced in order to rase the rating of the line. Cost: $5.5 M • Waverly Reactor 138 kV: Install a 4% series reactor towards Rozelle at Waverly station to address a N-1-0 scenario related to the loss of a nearby 345 kV line. Cost: $3.0 M • Saint Clair Avenue Reactor 138 kV: Adjust tap settings on reactors towards Mound and Clinton stations to 3%. Cost: $0.0 M • Marion Station: Replace switch and line riser at Marion station towards Obetz to address loading concern under certain N-1-1 scenario related to customer interconnections in the area. $0.1M

Construct (2) 138 kV tie lines to the customers dead end structures ~0.04 miles utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor SE 284 MVA. Cost: $9.54 M • Brie – Innovation 138 kV Tie: Construct a greenfield ~1.75 mile of double circuit line, utilizing 2-bundled ACSS Curlew 1033.5 (54/7) conductor, connecting Brie and Innovation stations as well as re-establish the Babbitt - Kirk 138 kV circuit. At Brie 138 kV station will install four 138 kV circuit breakers in two partial strings breaker and half configuration along with a 69.1 MVAR capacitor. Perform remote end work at Innovation, Babbitt, and Kirk 138 kV stations. This project addresses a consequential (for a N-1-1 contingency) load drop event of more than 300 MW for the loads served out of AEP’s Anguin and Brie stations while also addressing an overload on the Babbitt – Innovation 138 kV circuit in relation to new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $10.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Corridor – Vassell 345 kV #1 & #2 Circuits Sag Re-rate: Replace two structures to mitigate sag issues on the line in order to allow the line to operate to its conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.88 M • Kiber Station 138 kV: Cut-into Green Chapel – Corridor 138 kV circuit to a new Kiber station with (8 3) 80 kA 138 kV circuit breakers laid out in a breaker and a half arrangement to install a 300 2x150 MVAR STATCOM to support the significant amount of load added to the area. Cost: $35 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering analysis it was determined that in order to be able to physically accommodate the line exits along with two feeds to the STATCOM when taking into account future needs at the station that a total of 8 138 kV breakers would need to be installed initially. • Green Chapel Cap Banks 138 kV: Upgrade proposed cap banks at Green Chapel station from (2) 69.1 MVAR to (2) 115.2 MVAR. Cost: $3.6 M • Corridor 138 kV: Replace (12) 63 kA circuit breakers & cap breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $12.6 M • Babbitt 138 kV: Replace (2) 63 kA bus-tie circuit breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $2.15 M • Jug Street: Replace CB-C which is an existing 40 kA breaker with a 4000A 80kA 138 kV breaker to address interrupting capability concerns related to the introduction of the new 345 kV source at Innovation. Cost: $0.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Anchor Hocking – Lancaster 69 kV line Rebuild: Rebuild ~1.16 miles of 69 kV line utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor, SE 142 MVA. As a result of the new customer interconnections in the area, this line will overload under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Newark Center 138 kV: Install high and low side sectionalizing on the 138/69 kV transformer to address overloading of 69 kV lines in the area related to the new customer interconnections under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Fremont – West Fremont Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit & upgrade 1200 A switches at Fremont to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $2.0 M • Fremont – Fremont Center Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $1.5 M • Dumont 765 kV: Replace 3000 A circuit breaker at Dumont to address a generation deliverability violation on the Dumont – Sorenson 765 kV branch related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $4.0 M The following components are system reinforcements that were initially identified by AEP and later confirmed by PJM through their DNH analysis: • Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Green Chapel stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell – Curleys 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Curleys stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell 765 & 345 kV stations: Add 3-345 kV breakers to connect new lines to Curleys and Green Chapel. Cost: $10 M • Green Chapel 345/138 kV station: Install two 675 MVA, 345/138 kV transformers to connect the new Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line to 138 kV system and to mitigate overloading on the other 345/138 kV transformers in the system. Cost: $39.2 M System Upgrades: $199.2 M

sourceEvidence.name: PJM M-3 AEP-2023-OH019 row 679
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 679; Need Number AEP-2023-OH019; Need Meeting Date 2023-02-07 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2023-12-05 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3442; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: Customer Service: • A customer has requested transmission service at a site north of AEP’s existing Jug Street station in New Albany, OH. • The customer has indicated that their initial and ultimate peak demand will be 337 MW at the site. • The customer has requested an ISD of 12/15/2025; Solution Description: The following work is all direct connect facilities to physically connect demand to the grid. • Bermuda 345 kV: Reroute the Corridor – Innovation 345 kV circuit across the customer’s site utilizing 2-bundled ACSR Falcon 1590 (54/19) conductor, built with double circuit structures, SE rating 2278 MVA, to a new 345 kV Bermuda station with (11) 5000 A, 63kA circuit breakers & (1) 158.4 MVAR 345 kV Cap bank, laid out as breaker and a half configuration. Construct four single circuit lines ~0.1 miles, between Bermuda station and the customer; utilizing 2-bundle ACSR Drake 795 (26/7) conductor SE 1800 MVA. Cost: $60.3 M $58.3 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering reviews it was determined that the previously proposed capacitor bank at Bermuda would be more efficiently accommodated at Curleys station. The scope update adds the 2nd capacitor at Curleys and removes it from the scope at Bermuda. The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Corridor – Vassell 345 kV #1 & #2 Circuits Sag Re-rate: Replace two structures to mitigate sag issues on the line in order to allow the line to operate to its conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.88 M • Kiber Station 138 kV: Cut-into Green Chapel – Corridor 138 kV circuit to a new Kiber station with (8 3) 80 kA 138 kV circuit breakers laid out in a breaker and a half arrangement to install a 300 2x150 MVAR STATCOM to support the significant amount of load added to the area. Cost: $35 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering analysis it was determined that in order to be able to physically accommodate the line exits along with two feeds to the STATCOM when taking into account future needs at the station that a total of 8 138 kV breakers would need to be installed initially. • Green Chapel Cap Banks 138 kV: Upgrade proposed cap banks at Green Chapel station from (2) 69.1 MVAR to (2) 115.2 MVAR. Cost: $3.6 M • Corridor 138 kV: Replace (12) 63 kA circuit breakers & cap breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $12.6 M • Babbitt 138 kV: Replace (2) 63 kA bus-tie circuit breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $2.15 M • Jug Street: Replace CB-C which is an existing 40 kA breaker with a 4000A 80kA 138 kV breaker to address interrupting capability concerns related to the introduction of the new 345 kV source at Innovation. Cost: $0.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Anchor Hocking – Lancaster 69 kV line Rebuild: Rebuild ~1.16 miles of 69 kV line utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor, SE 142 MVA. As a result of the new customer interconnections in the area, this line will overload under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Newark Center 138 kV: Install high and low side sectionalizing on the 138/69 kV transformer to address overloading of 69 kV lines in the area related to the new customer interconnections under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Fremont – West Fremont Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit & upgrade 1200 A switches at Fremont to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $2.0 M • Fremont – Fremont Center Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $1.5 M • Dumont 765 kV: Replace 3000 A circuit breaker at Dumont to address a generation deliverability violation on the Dumont – Sorenson 765 kV branch related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $4.0 M The following components are system reinforcements that were initially identified by AEP and later confirmed by PJM through their DNH analysis: • Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Green Chapel stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell – Curleys 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Curleys stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell 765 & 345 kV stations: Add 3-345 kV breakers to connect new lines to Curleys and Green Chapel. Cost: $10 M • Green Chapel 345/138 kV station: Install two 675 MVA, 345/138 kV transformers to connect the new Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line to 138 kV system and to mitigate overloading on the other 345/138 kV transformers in the system. Cost: $39.2 M System Upgrades: $199.2 M

Install two 675MVA-345/138 kV power transformers. Install (6) 138kV, 63 kA, 4000 A breakers & (2) 69.1 MVAR 138 kV Cap bank on low side configured as ring bus with provisions for future breaker and half configuration. Structures will be replaced on the line to address distribution clearance issue in order to allow the lines to operate to their conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.5 M • Dublin Reactor 138 kV: Install a 4% series reactor towards Sawmill at Dublin station to address a N-1-1 scenario as a result of the new load interconnections in the area. Cost: $3.0 M

sourceEvidence.name: PJM M-3 AEP-2023-OH052 row 698
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 698; Need Number AEP-2023-OH052; Need Meeting Date 2023-04-21 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2023-12-05 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year 2024; PJM Upgrade ID s3442; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: An existing customer served out of AEP’s Anguin Station in New Albany, OH, has requested an additional service for a new bulk load addition of 100 MW. This will bring the total load for the customers site to 450 MW with an ultimate capacity of up to 720 MW. • Customer requested in-service date of 3/31/2024.; Solution Description: The following work is all direct connect facilities to physically connect demand to the grid. • Anguin – Chinstrap 138 kV: Extend the 138 kV double circuit line to Rockhopper by ~0.22 miles to the new Chinstrap (customer) station. Cost: $1.01 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Corridor – Vassell 345 kV #1 & #2 Circuits Sag Re-rate: Replace two structures to mitigate sag issues on the line in order to allow the line to operate to its conductor’s designed maximum operating temperature. Cost: $1.88 M • Kiber Station 138 kV: Cut-into Green Chapel – Corridor 138 kV circuit to a new Kiber station with (8 3) 80 kA 138 kV circuit breakers laid out in a breaker and a half arrangement to install a 300 2x150 MVAR STATCOM to support the significant amount of load added to the area. Cost: $35 M Reason For Update: As part of further engineering analysis it was determined that in order to be able to physically accommodate the line exits along with two feeds to the STATCOM when taking into account future needs at the station that a total of 8 138 kV breakers would need to be installed initially. • Green Chapel Cap Banks 138 kV: Upgrade proposed cap banks at Green Chapel station from (2) 69.1 MVAR to (2) 115.2 MVAR. Cost: $3.6 M • Corridor 138 kV: Replace (12) 63 kA circuit breakers & cap breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $12.6 M • Babbitt 138 kV: Replace (2) 63 kA bus-tie circuit breakers with 80 kA circuit breakers to improve interrupting capabilities as a result of the new sources in the area. Cost: $2.15 M • Jug Street: Replace CB-C which is an existing 40 kA breaker with a 4000A 80kA 138 kV breaker to address interrupting capability concerns related to the introduction of the new 345 kV source at Innovation. Cost: $0.8 M The following components are system reinforcements required to serve the load and meet applicable TPL-001, PJM, and AEP planning criteria: • Anchor Hocking – Lancaster 69 kV line Rebuild: Rebuild ~1.16 miles of 69 kV line utilizing ACSR Dove 556.5 (26/7) conductor, SE 142 MVA. As a result of the new customer interconnections in the area, this line will overload under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Newark Center 138 kV: Install high and low side sectionalizing on the 138/69 kV transformer to address overloading of 69 kV lines in the area related to the new customer interconnections under certain N-1-1 scenarios. Cost: $2.5 M • Fremont – West Fremont Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit & upgrade 1200 A switches at Fremont to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $2.0 M • Fremont – Fremont Center Sag re-rate 138 kV: Sag re-rate the 138 kV circuit to address a Generation deliverability violation related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $1.5 M • Dumont 765 kV: Replace 3000 A circuit breaker at Dumont to address a generation deliverability violation on the Dumont – Sorenson 765 kV branch related to the new customer interconnections in the area. Cost: $4.0 M The following components are system reinforcements that were initially identified by AEP and later confirmed by PJM through their DNH analysis: • Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Green Chapel stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell – Curleys 345 kV line: Install approximately 12.5-mile long 345 kV transmission between Vassell and Curleys stations to mitigate overloading on multiple transmission facilities including other 345 kV transmission lines and 345-138 kV transformers. Cost: $75.0 M • Vassell 765 & 345 kV stations: Add 3-345 kV breakers to connect new lines to Curleys and Green Chapel. Cost: $10 M • Green Chapel 345/138 kV station: Install two 675 MVA, 345/138 kV transformers to connect the new Vassell – Green Chapel 345 kV line to 138 kV system and to mitigate overloading on the other 345/138 kV transformers in the system. Cost: $39.2 M System Upgrades: $199.2 M

judgements.rationale: APS-2023-029의 명시 지원설비에서 s3150.1=EP, s3150.2=IS가 확인된다. 계통 설계·조달/계획 진행을 반영하고 고객 IA 체결이나 실제 공사로 간주하지 않는다.
assumptions: 다섯 요건별 진행률은 공개 근거를 바탕으로 고른 정성 단계 모형의 가정이다. 고객 계약·인허가·통전 승인을 모두 직접 확인한 것은 아니다.
개별 고객 접속 요청과 해당 고객을 지원하는 계통 설비의 진행을 구분한다.
현재 공개된 취소되지 않은 개별 요청에서 최근 갱신된 진행 중 계통설비 상태를 근거로 아직 진행 중인 신청/확장으로 추정한다. 고객의 현재 활성 확인서에 해당하지 않는다.
limitations: M-3 Need ID는 고객 ISO 큐 ID가 아니라 해당 고객 요청에 따른 송전계획 식별자다.

새로 확보한 XML은 현재 공개된 상태를 제공하나 행별 LastUpdated와 실제 InServiceDate는 다르다.
일부 지원설비의 실제 통전일이 존재하지만 고객 전체 운영·계약용량 통전 비율로 환산하지 않았다.

고객 원장의 주가 비어 있어 원문 지명 또는 동일 접속 지점의 위치 자료를 별도 대조했습니다. 고객 Need의 정확한 보강 ID로 연결된 접속 지점/로컬 공급 설비 s3150.2가 XML State=MD로 표시된다. XML Description이 customer/delivery point/service point를 직접 지칭한다. 연결된 설비들의 주가 모두 일치하며 remote-end 항목만으로 고객 주를 추정하지 않았다.

sourceEvidence.name: PJM M-3 Dayton-2019-009 row 1583
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 1583; Need Number Dayton-2019-009; Need Meeting Date 2019-10-25 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2019-12-18 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date 2020-02-03 00:00:00; Local Plan Year 2020; PJM Upgrade ID s2150; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: An new industrial customer has requested a new delivery point in Brookville, Ohio. The potential customer site is located north of Upper Lewisburg Salem Rd and west of Arlington Rd in close proximity to the existing 6639 transmission line. The route of the existing 6639 line is shown in the graphic on the right side of the slide.-Prior to the need for full transmission capacity, the customer will require 500kW of capacity immediately to begin construction activities. By April 1, 2020 the customer will require a minimum of 5MW of total capacity to finalize building construction and the installation of production equipment. By November of 2020, the full substation and capacity for an 11MVA load will be required. There are long-terms plan for the customer to potentially grow to a 26MVA load.-In order to support the customer’s delivery needs, support local economic development, and maintain system reliability for all customers, it is necessary to promptly begin designing and building a comprehensive solution that can supply the customer needs and meet the schedule outlined in this slide.; Solution Description: Dayton has developed a comprehensive distribution and transmission solution to meet both the short-term and long term needs identified in problem statement. Dayton plans to install distribution level service to provide service to the first 500 kW and 5 MW loads. The transmission project to serve the initial 11 MVA of load will entail tapping the existing Brookville-West Manchester 69 kV line (6639). This new transmission tap, constructed with 477 ACSR conductor, will loop in and out of a new three-breaker 69 kV ring bus substation where one (1) 69/12 kV 30 MVA transformer will be installed. Fiber will be added from Brookville Substation to the new sub, so remote end relay changes will be needed at Brookville Substation. Remote end relay setting updates will be required at West Manchester substation.

judgements.rationale: DOM-2020-0043의 exact ID 지원설비 중 s2622.1가 UC(공사 진행)이다. 고객 접속에 필요한 설비 공사 진척을 40점 정성 모형에 반영한다. 고객 계약 전체/최종 운영 승인을 확인했다는 뜻은 아니다.
assumptions: 다섯 요건별 진행률은 공개 근거를 바탕으로 고른 정성 단계 모형의 가정이다. 고객 계약·인허가·통전 승인을 모두 직접 확인한 것은 아니다.
개별 고객 접속 요청과 해당 고객을 지원하는 계통 설비의 진행을 구분한다.
현재 공개된 취소되지 않은 개별 요청에서 최근 갱신된 진행 중 계통설비 상태를 근거로 아직 진행 중인 신청/확장으로 추정한다. 고객의 현재 활성 확인서에 해당하지 않는다.
limitations: M-3 Need ID는 고객 ISO 큐 ID가 아니라 해당 고객 요청에 따른 송전계획 식별자다.
보강계획 목표일이 지났다는 이유로 고객 운영·미진행·정체를 추정하지 않는다.
새로 확보한 XML은 현재 공개된 상태를 제공하나 행별 LastUpdated와 실제 InServiceDate는 다르다.
일부 지원설비의 실제 통전일이 존재하지만 고객 전체 운영·계약용량 통전 비율로 환산하지 않았다.
고객 원장의 주가 비어 있어 원문 지명 또는 동일 접속 지점의 위치 자료를 별도 대조했습니다. 고객 Problem Statement에 Fairfax County가 명시되며 Census 전국 명부의 같은 카운티 이름이 단일 주 VA에만 존재한다. 유틸리티 서비스영역으로 추정하지 않았다.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Tracking Sheet row 2253; Need Number EKPC-2025-001; Need Meeting Date 2025-03-04 00:00:00; Solution Meeting Date 2025-05-06 00:00:00; Local Plan Posting Date None; Local Plan Year None; PJM Upgrade ID None; Withdrawal/Cancellation None; Status Notes None; Problem Statement: A new customer has requested transmission service in Mason County, KY. The initial load is expected to be 110 MW by 12/2026. With a load ramp schedule as follows: 530 MW by 2/2028 850 MW by 8/2028 2200 MW by 1/2031; Solution Description: The customer will initially take distribution service for construction power. The potential transmission solution requires work to be performed by two utilities, East Kentucky Power Cooperative (EKPC) and Dayton Power & Light (DP&L) to meet the customers time line and load ramp schedule. The potential solution will consist of four phases the first (Phase 0) being temporary enables EKPC to meet the requested load ramp schedule and provide service to the customer quickly. The overall plan for the potential solution involves looping in the existing Spurlock – North Clark 345 kV line, constructing two new 345 kV lines from EKPC’s Spurlock Station and two new 345 kV lines from DP&L’s Stuart substation to the site. Within the site, a campus of three 345/138 kV switching stations will provide the customer service at 138 kV. These three substations within the campus will be configured in a “ring” configuration to provide ties within the campus in the event of loss of sources into each of the substations. Phase 0: Construct two ~1.5 miles 138 kV temporary tap lines to extend from the Spurlock - Goddard 138 kV and Spurlock - Plumville 138 kV lines. Customer to take 138 kV service. Phase 1: Construct a new 345/138 kV switching station (Mason County 1) with six 3000 A, 63 kA, 345 kV circuit breakers and fifteen 3000 A, 63 kA, 138 kV breakers and two 345/138 kV transformers. EKPC will intercept the Spurlock - North Clark 345 kV line and extend it approximately 1.5 miles into the new substation Mason County 1. Phase 2: Expand the Mason County 1 345/138 kV station and install three addition 3000 A, 63 kA, 345 kV circuit breakers and eleven additional 3000 A, 63 kA, 138 kV breakers and one additional 345/138 kV transformer. Construct a new 345/138 kV switching station (Mason County 2) with eight 3000 A, 63 kA, 345 kV circuit breakers and six 3000 A, 63 kA, 138 kV breakers and two 345/138 kV transformers. Construct a new approximately 4.0-mile 345 kV double circuit from EKPC’s Spurlock. Terminating on side at Mason County 1 and the other at Mason County 2. Break the existing Mason County 1- North Clark 345 kV line and re-terminate the North Clark side at Mason County 2. Repurpose the remaining portion of the line as a tie between Mason County 1 and Mason County 2. Phase 3: Expand the Mason County 2 345/138 kV station and install three addition 3000 A, 63 kA, 345kV circuit breakers and fourteen additional 3000 A, 63 kA, 138kV breakers and one additional 345/138 kV transformer. Construct a new 345/138 kV switching station (Mason County 3) with eight 3000 A, 63 kA, 345kV circuit breakers and seventeen 3000 A, 63 kA, 138kV breakers and two 345/138 kV transformers. Construct a new approximately 11.0-mile 345 kV double circuit from DP&L’s Stuart station. Terminating on side at Mason County 2 and the other at Mason County 3. Remove temporary Phase 0 construction. Total load to be served from the 345/138 kV stations.

judgements.rationale: JCPL-2020-006의 명시 지원설비에서 s2358=EP가 확인된다. 계통 설계·조달/계획 진행을 반영하고 고객 IA 체결이나 실제 공사로 간주하지 않는다.
assumptions: 다섯 요건별 진행률은 공개 근거를 바탕으로 고른 정성 단계 모형의 가정이다. 고객 계약·인허가·통전 승인을 모두 직접 확인한 것은 아니다.
개별 고객 접속 요청과 해당 고객을 지원하는 계통 설비의 진행을 구분한다.
현재 공개된 취소되지 않은 개별 요청에서 최근 갱신된 진행 중 계통설비 상태를 근거로 아직 진행 중인 신청/확장으로 추정한다. 고객의 현재 활성 확인서에 해당하지 않는다.
limitations: M-3 Need ID는 고객 ISO 큐 ID가 아니라 해당 고객 요청에 따른 송전계획 식별자다.
보강계획 목표일이 지났다는 이유로 고객 운영·미진행·정체를 추정하지 않는다.
새로 확보한 XML은 현재 공개된 상태를 제공하나 행별 LastUpdated와 실제 InServiceDate는 다르다.

고객 원장의 주가 비어 있어 원문 지명 또는 동일 접속 지점의 위치 자료를 별도 대조했습니다. 고객 Need의 정확한 보강 ID로 연결된 접속 지점/로컬 공급 설비 s2358가 XML State=NJ로 표시된다. XML Location이 고객 문제 설명에 직접 등장한다. 연결된 설비들의 주가 모두 일치하며 remote-end 항목만으로 고객 주를 추정하지 않았다.
judgements.identityRationale: 현재 canonical ID request:pjm-m3-jcpl-2020-006-r2297의 정확한 원문 요청 ID/고객·부지를 사용한다. 회사 이름이나 지역 일치만으로 다른 부지와 연결하지 않는다. 위치 검토: 고객 Need의 정확한 보강 ID로 연결된 접속 지점/로컬 공급 설비 s2358가 XML State=NJ로 표시된다. XML Location이 고객 문제 설명에 직접 등장한다. 연결된 설비들의 주가 모두 일치하며 remote-end 항목만으로 고객 주를 추정하지 않았다. 원문 PJM_M3_JCPL_2020_006는 참고 기록으로 보존하고 동일 고객 요청의 CENSUS::request:pjm-m3-jcpl-2020-006-r2297만 평균에 반영합니다.

개별 고객 접속 요청과 해당 고객을 지원하는 계통 설비의 진행을 구분한다.
현재 공개된 취소되지 않은 개별 요청에서 최근 갱신된 진행 중 계통설비 상태를 근거로 아직 진행 중인 신청/확장으로 추정한다. 고객의 현재 활성 확인서에 해당하지 않는다.

judgements.rationale: PPL-2026-0016에 대해 2026-04-14 해결안 회의와 고객 관련 구체적인 설비 대안이 제시됐다. 기술 접속설계 단계로 추정한다.
assumptions: 다섯 요건별 진행률은 공개 근거를 바탕으로 고른 정성 단계 모형의 가정이다. 고객 계약·인허가·통전 승인을 모두 직접 확인한 것은 아니다.
개별 고객 접속 요청과 해당 고객을 지원하는 계통 설비의 진행을 구분한다.
현재 공개된 취소되지 않은 개별 요청에서 2027년 이후 구체적 고객 공급/보강 일정를 근거로 아직 진행 중인 신청/확장으로 추정한다. 고객의 현재 활성 확인서에 해당하지 않는다.
limitations: M-3 Need ID는 고객 ISO 큐 ID가 아니라 해당 고객 요청에 따른 송전계획 식별자다.
보강계획 목표일이 지났다는 이유로 고객 운영·미진행·정체를 추정하지 않는다.
새로 확보한 XML은 현재 공개된 상태를 제공하나 행별 LastUpdated와 실제 InServiceDate는 다르다.
judgements.identityRationale: 현재 canonical ID request:pjm-m3-ppl-2026-0016-r2964의 정확한 원문 요청 ID/고객·부지를 사용한다. 회사 이름이나 지역 일치만으로 다른 부지와 연결하지 않는다. 원문 PJM_M3_PPL_2026_0016는 참고 기록으로 보존하고 동일 고객 요청의 CENSUS::request:pjm-m3-ppl-2026-0016-r2964만 평균에 반영합니다.

The power delivery schedule will ramp over time, expecting to achieve the full volume no later than 2032, with the potential to meaningfully accelerate. sourceEvidence.name: Ohio Tech News: Google testimony before Ohio Joint Data Center Committee
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Google has invested more than $20 billion in its Ohio data center operations since 2019, company leaders told state lawmakers last week — and says that footprint is helping put “downward pressure” on electric rates for households and small businesses across the state. Liz Schwab, market development and policy manager for Google Data Centers, made the case before the Ohio Joint Data Center Committee at a historic hearing that brought all four of the world’s largest hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft — to the Statehouse, a lineup committee co-chair Rep. Adam Holmes called “perhaps unprecedented.” Why it matters Ohio has become one of the country’s fastest-growing data center markets, and the industry’s biggest players are showing up — answering nearly six hours of lawmakers’ questions and laying out what their growth delivers for Ohioans today and over the long term. By the numbers $20 billion+ invested across Central Ohio by Google in New Albany, Columbus and Lancaster 3,000 full-time operational employees $125,000 median cash compensation 9 additional Ohio jobs supported for every direct data center job Good for ratepayers Schwab told lawmakers Google buys 100% of its Ohio power through competitive markets under PUCO-approved tariffs — and pledged the company will keep “paying our own way” as a responsible steward of shared infrastructure. Her argument: a large, steady load lets utilities spread fixed costs across a wider base, helping hold down rates for Ohio families and small businesses rather than shifting costs onto them. Google is backing that up with a first-of-its-kind initiative to aggregate 100 megawatts of distributed capacity annually into a virtual power plant on the PJM grid. 개별 고객 접속 요청과 해당 고객을 지원하는 계통 설비의 진행을 구분한다.
limitations: M-3 Need ID는 고객 ISO 큐 ID가 아니라 해당 고객 요청에 따른 송전계획 식별자다.
보강계획 목표일이 지났다는 이유로 고객 운영·미진행·정체를 추정하지 않는다.
새로 확보한 XML은 현재 공개된 상태를 제공하나 행별 LastUpdated와 실제 InServiceDate는 다르다.
익명 M-3 AEP-2022-AP014와 같은 사업일 가능성이 있어 두 행을 동시에 평균에 넣지 않는다.
judgements.identityRationale: 현재 canonical ID site:pjm-wvpsc-23-0865-e-pc-nucor-apple-grove의 정확한 원문 요청 ID/고객·부지를 사용한다. 중복 가능성 request:pjm-m3-aep-2022-ap014-r516는 미해소되어 평균 권고에서 제외한다. 기존 개별 신청 원장을 평균 대표로 유지하고, 같은 사업일 수 있는 익명 후보는 평균에서 제외했습니다. 후보의 물리적 동일성이 확정됐다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

실명 PECO 담당자 발언을 인용한 현장 보도에서 take-or-pay 공급계약, 6월 첫 PECO 연결 구간 통전, 첫 100만 sqft 건물 공사 및 2026Q4 첫 운영 목표가 함께 확인된다. 하지만 canonical은 여러 해에 걸쳐 추가 건물을 짓는 전체 250-acre 캠퍼스다. 초기 구간의 통전을 전체 캠퍼스 보강 완료로 확장하지 않고 고객시설 건설·전체 계통공사 미확인 55점으로 추정한다.
Salem/Susquehanna 인접 Amazon 캠퍼스는 기존 공동입지 공급에서 PJM front-of-meter로 전환하기 위한 송전 재구성이 공식 공시에 명시된다. 기존 운영과 신규 확장이 섞여 있으며 1,920MW PPA는 다른 PA 부지에도 공급할 수 있어 단일 신청 용량/완료계약으로 보지 않는다. 공개 계통 전환 계획 위치로 65점을 추정한다.
Cipher 공식 발표는 Ulysses 195에이커 단일 Ohio 부지의 AEP Ohio 200MW 확보 용량 및 필요한 모든 유틸리티 계약 체결을 명시한다. 2026-02-24 IR도 PJM 승인 접속과 2027Q4 통전 목표를 재확인한다. 계약 단계 50점으로 평가한다.
개발사 공식 발표가 CoreWeave의 Lancaster 캠퍼스 임차·투자와 건설, PPL과의 약 2억 달러 지역 계통 투자를 연결한다. 부지 건설이 진행된 정성 위치를 55점으로 평가하되 고객별 전력계약·계통 공사 완료를 확인한 것으로 보지 않는다.
FERC는 PECO–Amazon Transmission Security Agreement를 수리했다. 계약 단계 50점은 가능하지만 이 계약의 정확한 부지 범위를 원문에서 식별하지 못해 Falls Township과 자동 병합하거나 활성 분모를 추가하지 않는다.
Columbus 5076 South High Street를 특정한 2026-08-17 프로젝트 표가 Under construction으로 명시한다. 공식 Google 위치 페이지와 2026년 주의회 증언 보도를 대조해 부지 건설 단계 55점으로 추정한다. 계통설비 공사는 미확인이다.
Lancaster 105 Whiley Road를 특정한 2026-08-17 건설 보도는 첫 건물이 2024년 완료됐고 전체 캠퍼스 개발은 계속된다고 구분한다. 추가 개발의 건설 위치 55점은 제시하되 기존 운영과 신규 신청 구분이 안 되어 활성 평균에서 제외한다.
공식 고객 페이지가 New Albany 시설을 식별하고, 2026년 프로젝트별 건설 보도는 New Albany가 finished라고 구분한다. 2026년 주의회 증언 보도도 Ohio 운영 인력/전력구매를 확인하므로 기존 부지 운영으로 추정한다. 신규 확장 단위는 분리 미확인이라 활성 신청 평균에서 제외한다.
Muskie 단일 캠퍼스는 2026-10-05 Kentucky Power와 전력 서비스 계약을 1GW로 개정 체결했다. PSC 승인과 유틸리티 공사 일정이 남아 있어 계약 단계 50점으로 평가한다.
Virginia SCC 사건의 Microsoft Boydton 증언이 기존 운영 고객임을 확인한다. 현재 신규 확장 신청과 분리하여 활성 신청 점수/평균에 포함하지 않는다.
